## Start here

1. **Summary:** [Summary](00-overview/summary.md). Synergon supports work environment layout, design and evaluation, organised as Workspace → Project → Scene. Its first example is a photo-estimated remote operator’s station with an adjustable rig and a seated person, placed in scenes that people and AI agents edit together.
2. **Lessons learned:** [Lessons learned](60-lessons/lessons-learned.md). Fifty-five numbered lessons (L-01 to L-55) from building a 3D asset from photos with a team of AI agents, each one sentence with its evidence and how it is now applied, grouped by topic, with a top ten and a map to the failures and patterns behind them.
3. **Model card:** [Model card of the Rig B asset](70-results/rig-b-model-card.md). What the Rig B asset is, what it is for and what it must not be used for - 46 parts in five groups, 20 joints (6 of them assumed), 14 reference frames and 305 parameter records with their sources and ranges, built from eleven photos; sizes are photo estimates never checked against a tape, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos.
4. **Next steps:** [Next steps](90-next/next-steps.md). What to do next, in priority order and by whom: platform step 1 is live (2026-11-24) and the owner tries it; then a tape session with four questions for the owner, a planted-error test of the reviewer, the Skill on a second object, small fixes, other rig configurations, the assessment and simulator phases, and routine maintenance.

## Plan

- [The approved plan](30-plan/approved-plan.md): Version 3 of the plan, approved by the owner on 2026-11-23, rewritten for the wiki. It judged the task feasible as a structural, articulated, re-measurable layout model, with sizes and looks not yet shown, and set out a five-stage method built on parametric code, honest size ranges, scripted checks and an independent reviewer. *(stable, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Deviations from the approved plan](30-plan/deviations.md): What was done differently from the approved plan and why. The largest change is the owner's direction to run a full implementation autonomously, which replaced the plan's human gates, owner clicks and separate acceptance author with reviewer rounds and the coordinator's checks in the browser. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The platform plan (version 7)](30-plan/platform-plan.md): The second plan, approved by the owner on 2026-11-24, in plain words. It turns Synergon from one model into a working platform in five steps that can each be stopped after - agent control, honest numbers, assessment, an agent in the app, a control room - with an independent simplicity monitor. Step 1 is built; what it changed from the plan is listed here. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*

## Method

- [The agent process](40-method/agent-process.md): How the agents were organised in this run - a coordinator, an infrastructure agent, a measurement agent, three modellers in parallel, an independent reviewer, two interface reviewers and an implementer - what each brief contained, how collisions were avoided, and which parts of the approved process were not exercised. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The asset contract](40-method/asset-contract.md): What an asset must satisfy - units, axes, names, parameter records, spec, component modules, materials, GLB, description file, posing and budgets for the rig; and, in section 14, for a character asset (the manikin) - axes, joint names, skins, shape files, compression, budgets and credits. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Checks](40-method/checks.md): Every automatic check of the asset and the platform (bun run check, 28 checks, 8 of them added by platform step 1 for the commands, the server, the live page and the deploy), of the distribution build (2) and of the viewer page (53), with what each verifies, the real failure it exists to catch, and its current result; plus the host's load test, what is not checked and how to add a check. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Decomposition and connections](40-method/decomposition.md): How an object is split into components - one structural tree plus tags for function - how connections and pivots are established from photos and recorded, and the real tree of Rig B as built, with its 20 joints and 14 reference frames. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Filling gaps (augmentation)](40-method/filling-gaps.md): How values that the photos do not give are filled in, how each value says where it came from, what the build enforces so invented values cannot pass as measured, and how a real measurement overrides an estimate. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Manikin approaches](40-method/manikin-approaches.md): Which body and character libraries were weighed for a seated ergonomic manikin that looks like a game character, follows the ANSUR II survey, bends like a game rig and runs in a browser. Commercial ones, MetaHuman included, are referenced only. The choice is the open MakeHuman mesh with a survey-fitted shape space and a game-style rig; both styles have passed the designer: the abstract style at level 3, the dressed style at level 4 minus at working distance; neither is MetaHuman quality. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Measuring from photos](40-method/measuring-from-photos.md): The measuring procedure as executed for Rig B - camera from metadata, structure from motion, bundle adjustment in a model frame fixed on the platform deck, scale closure against purchased parts, triangulation and single-view rays, honest classes and ranges, and what the photos cannot check. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The pipeline, end to end](40-method/pipeline.md): How eleven phone photos became a parametric, articulated 3D asset and a browser viewer; each stage with its inputs, outputs, command, who does it and how long it took on this machine. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*

## Implementation

- [Deployment](50-implementation/deployment.md): Every push to main deploys automatically; bun run deploy does the same by hand. It checks everything, builds the viewer, model, wiki and server into one release, uploads it through a restricted account, switches the site atomically, checks it over HTTPS at synergon.mightwork.ai and switches back on failure. The host's one-time setup, its service and the cutover from the earlier address are on a page of their own. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Live screen content](50-implementation/live-screen-content.md): The flat screens of a scene's assets can show a live web page instead of their built-in picture, such as a Leitbild scenario's displays on the operator desk or a YouTube clip on the wall display. The scene stores which screen shows what; every open viewer follows each change at once; people operate a screen with Use; agents configure everything with the content.* commands and read back what each viewer reports. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Measurement results](50-implementation/measurement-results.md): What the photos gave for Rig B - the scale closes within 0-2 % against purchased parts, five cameras were solved, 118 dimensions were recorded with a class and a range, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos. Nothing here has been checked against a tape measure. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Modelling rounds](50-implementation/modeling-rounds.md): The model's story in pictures - two planning trials that silently lacked the left pod, a complete blockout, a first formed model that the independent reviewer rejected as "in between" (8 of 45 components rejected), a second round that closed 24 of 28 findings and was accepted after three small fixes, and a third round of those fixes. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The person's commands](50-implementation/person-commands.md): The shared scene stores the seated person and its optional target IDs. One person command sets gaze, hands and feet, and the server and viewer solve them against the current rig. The server reports gaze alignment, contact gaps, reach and clearances. *(draft, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [The person in the viewer](50-implementation/person-in-viewer.md): The designer-passed manikin runs in the product viewer as its own script, loaded after the rig is ready (still 0.25 s and 748 kB of scripts); the dressed operator sits in the real rig 0.6 s later. Shader changes are confined to its materials (the rig's pictures are identical to main's to the pixel); it idles at 30 frames a second only in a live view; a frame costs 10 to 15 ms against 3 to 4 ms for the rig. *(draft, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [The person panel](50-implementation/person-panel.md): Click the seated person or choose Person from Components to show its controls in the left workspace panel. Edit the body and appearance, change the preset, and undo changes in the shared workspace. Settings → Credits lists the sources and licences. *(draft, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Portable room projects](50-implementation/portable-projects.md): Create a local project, restore named scene versions, and transfer exact asset releases and assessment inputs between installations. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Remote command design review](50-implementation/remote-command-design.md): Why the HTTP command contract stays canonical, what Synergon adopted from Leitbild, and when to evolve discovery, routing and the scene model. *(living, updated 2026-11-26)*
- [Scene editor](50-implementation/room-layout.md): Arrange a scene's room, edit its assets and operator, and discover the same instance-qualified controls through HTTP, MCP or the CLI. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [The Synergon server and its host setup](50-implementation/server-and-host-setup.md): The server on the production host - one hardened Bun service on 127.0.0.1:4191 behind one Caddy site for synergon.mightwork.ai, installed once by a reviewed setup script with fourteen host checks. The setup for the new address is prepared and tested locally; it has not been run on the host yet. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Tech stack as built](50-implementation/tech-stack.md): Bun and TypeScript, with three.js the only library that reaches the browser; Python reads the model file independently; headless Chromium makes every render. Since platform step 1 a small Bun server with no added package holds the shared scene (commands over HTTP, changes as server-sent events). Six pinned npm packages, all MIT or Apache-2.0; no Blender or photogrammetry. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Timeline and performance](50-implementation/timeline-and-performance.md): How long everything took on 2026-11-23, phase by phase - about 3.5 hours of planning with 16 agents, then 2 hours 46 minutes from the first implementation step to the round-2 verdict with 14 agent runs - with every agent run's duration, tokens and tool calls, the measured run times of every tool, and the model's size at each stage. All figures come from one Apple M2 machine and one run. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The viewer](50-implementation/viewer.md): The rig fills the viewer. Click a component or the seated person to edit it in the resizable left panel. The same panel holds the workspace selector, component list and Settings. Camera controls sit over the view. Live adjustments are shared and can be undone. *(living, updated 2026-11-26)*
- [Workspaces, projects and scenes](50-implementation/workspaces-projects-scenes.md): Synergon is organised as Workspace → Project → Scene on both installations. A scene is the live layout (room, placed assets, optional seated operator, undo history) and opens at /workspaces/{scene}. One folder-based store holds everything; the older single-station product and the separate room store are retired. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Single-station workspaces (retired)](50-implementation/workspaces.md): The server keeps many shared scenes, called workspaces, instead of one. Each has a random link, its own history and undo, its own live view, activity line and agent address. Anyone with a link can use, rename or delete it; making new ones is rate-limited; nothing is ever deleted for good by the server. Live on the public site since 2026-11-25. *(stable, updated 2026-11-27)*

## Results

- [Critique](70-results/critique.md): An honest list of what is weak in the result - the model (sizes never taped, depth seen from one viewpoint, borrowed left side, assumed adjustments and pivots), the method (no planted-error test of the reviewer, no human gates, one object and one run, builders and reviewers of one model family, scale resting on one spoken figure), the viewer, the documentation and the process. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Gallery](70-results/gallery.md): Every picture of the project in order - the eleven masked source photos by rig, the planning trials, the blockout, modelling rounds 1 to 3 with the reviewers' sheets, the final model from several views, the model laid over the photos, and the browser viewer before and after its redesign - each with a caption saying what to look at. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Goal assessment](70-results/goal-assessment.md): Of the first 69 requirements, 55 are met, 11 partly, none not met and 3 not yet done (GitHub and the production wiki). The run shows a credible, modular, parametric, articulated model built from casual photos by AI agents, with honest provenance; it does not show that the sizes are right or that the Skill transfers to another object. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Three people in Rig B](70-results/people-in-rig-b.md): The package's three presets (P5 woman, P50 man, P95 man) seated in the real rig, with a heavier test body beside them: the 0.47 m seat is too deep for the P5 woman and the pedals 12 cm beyond her feet as photographed, the P95 man's hips meet the armrest pods, every grip is in reach, and the monitor's top edge stands 10 to 24 cm above every eye; the sizes are photo estimates. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
- [Model card of the Rig B asset](70-results/rig-b-model-card.md): What the Rig B asset is, what it is for and what it must not be used for - 46 parts in five groups, 20 joints (6 of them assumed), 14 reference frames and 305 parameter records with their sources and ranges, built from eleven photos; sizes are photo estimates never checked against a tape, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*

## Operator desk

- [Operator desk: a second object built from photos](75-operator-desk/overview.md): A control-room desk with five screens was turned into a 3D model with named, movable parts from 15 phone photos and 21 measuring-app screenshots in one evening. It is recognisable and good enough for room layout; its sizes are unverified (probably within 2–4 %) and its motions are assumed. Ten tape readings would change that. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*
- [How the desk was modelled, step by step](75-operator-desk/how-it-was-done.md): The desk went from photos to a finished model in twelve steps - look at every photo, set the scale from a metre rule, measure by crossing sight lines, list the parts, build everything as plain boxes, have a stranger review it, shape it, review again, and audit the method. Each step is shown with its picture, and so is every correction made on the way. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*
- [Desk measurements and accuracy](75-operator-desk/measurements-and-accuracy.md): Every size of the desk model comes from the photos, scaled by one metre rule; none has been checked with a tape. The large visible sizes are probably within 2–4 % (overall width 2.41 m ± 0.07 m). The phone's measuring app was good to about ±3 cm at best and up to 17 % off; the height travel and all screen tilts are assumed. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*
- [Desk reviews, method changes, lessons](75-operator-desk/review-and-lessons.md): Three fresh reviewers accepted the desk model with minor fixes and found, in every round, things the builder could not see. Two auditors then showed that the record claimed more accuracy than it had tested, that some values had been set to satisfy a check, and that nobody had judged the sizes independently. The model card, the record and the written method were corrected; twelve lessons follow. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*
- [Photo guide: documenting an object for modelling](75-operator-desk/photo-guide.md): The 36 images were enough for a recognisable, well-divided model but not for verified sizes, angles or motions. The result rests on 15 of them; 19 were not needed and 9 useful views were missing. Next time - a rule in the picture (flat, front to back, upright), original files, the whole object from each corner and square-on, each moving part in two positions, and ten tape readings. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*
- [Questions for the site about the desk](75-operator-desk/questions-for-the-site.md): Three questions only the site can answer (does the top rise and what rises with it, how deep is the canopy, are the screen tilts adjustable) and the ten tape readings that would turn the desk model's estimates into measurements - about ten minutes at the desk with a tape and a phone. *(living, updated 2026-11-27)*

- [Skills and agents](80-reference/skills-and-agents.md): The Agent Skill "modeling-3d-assets-from-references" (version 0.1.0) and three agent definitions that package the modelling method for the next asset, and the operating Skill "operating-synergon" (v3) that tells Claude Code how to find, change, measure and undo things in a scene; what each holds, how to invoke it, what is unexercised and how the Skills are refined. *(living, updated 2026-11-28)*
- [Research sources](80-reference/sources.md): One short section for each of the sixteen documents behind the plan (eight specialist reports, two critiques, five adversarial reviews, one closure check), giving the question it answered, what it established with the key numbers, what it could not verify, and which wiki pages carry its content. The full texts are in the project's private archive. *(stable, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Human-factors standards and the seat reference](80-reference/standards.md): Which ergonomic standards bear on a seated remote-operation station, as far as this project established it, what each would need from the 3D asset, and why the asset carries "estimated seat reference" frames instead of a standardised seat index point. No standard was read in full; every statement is marked read in part or recalled, and must be confirmed against purchased texts. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Tool reference](80-reference/tools.md): Every command of the project (build, check, render, serve, rig, dist, wiki, deploy; the acceptance, live and deploy tests; the setup script; the independent model reader) with its options, outputs and typical run time, plus the shared scene's commands, the viewer's URL and script interface, the build folders and where every output goes. *(living, updated 2026-11-25)*
